summary: Feed s157_double is degraded: IDS faces 12.4% duplicate traffic and severe overload (3.02 Gbps bursts vs 1 Gbps port, 302% capacity). Both reduce detection coverage and must be fixed with broker deduplication and load balancing.

findings.root_cause: 12.4% duplicates (230 of 1851 packets) indicates the packet broker is forwarding the same packet twice, typically from overlapping SPAN/mirror sessions or dual TAP feeds aggregated without deduplication. IDS is seeing identical copies of the same frames.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes CPU and throughput re-processing duplicates, inflates flow counts, distorts TCP stream reassembly and can cause false-positive correlations and missed true positives due to state table pressure.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to drop identical packets within a short time window before delivery, eliminating the 12% overhead while preserving all unique flows for full-payload inspection.

findings.root_cause: Peak bursts of 3.02 Gbps in 1 ms intervals exceed the IDS 1 Gbps port by 302% (3 overloaded intervals). Broker is delivering line-rate bursts directly to a single tool port with no load-balancing, shaping, or burst buffering.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC buffers overrun and silently drops packets during bursts. With needs_both_directions=true and needs_full_payload=true, drops break TCP reassembly and cause blind spots - attacks in bursts are missed entirely.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic flow-aware across multiple IDS ports/instances to keep per-port utilization below 80% of 1 Gbps, preserving both directions of each flow on the same tool for stateful IDS detection and absorbing microbursts.
